rules.title: Trust is kept per trust key
rules.statement: Trust state MUST be kept separately for each trust key (organisation, agent, task type) and MUST NOT be shared between keys.
rules.rationale: An agent can be reliable at one kind of work and unreliable at another. Trust per agent lets one weak task type hold back all the others.
rules.evidence: Trust per task type gave 27% automation against 7% for trust per agent, in simulation ([research/REPORT.md](../../research/REPORT.md), rule L3, tag `research/prereg`). Pooling evidence across an agent's task types penalised its good types ([research/REPORT-v1.md](../../research/REPORT-v1.md), V3, tag `research/prereg-v1`).
rules.notes: v0 found per-agent trust has fewer escapes per 100 actions (0.55 against 0.60) because it barely automates anything.

rules.title: Only judged actions are evidence
rules.statement: Only judged actions (pre-review outcomes, spot-check outcomes and incidents) MUST count as evidence, and autonomous actions nobody judged MUST NOT count as evidence of good work.
rules.rationale: Silence isn't approval.

rules.title: Pre-review and spot-check outcomes weigh the same
rules.statement: An outcome from a spot-check MUST carry the same weight as an outcome from a pre-review.
rules.rationale: Both are a person judging real work.
rules.evidence: The policy tested in every round weighs them equally ([research/REPORT.md](../../research/REPORT.md); [research/REPORT-v3.md](../../research/REPORT-v3.md)).

rules.title: What counts as a serious error
rules.statement: An outcome MUST count as a serious error when it is labelled `material_edit` or `rejected` with a serious reason code, or when it is an incident, and cosmetic edits and `incomplete` outcomes MUST NOT count as serious errors.
rules.rationale: Trust is about consequential mistakes: a wrong or unauthorised action, a made-up fact or amount, a promise the policy doesn't allow, or obeying an instruction hidden in a message. Wording and tone are taste.
rules.evidence: The definition used in every tier ([research/REPORT.md](../../research/REPORT.md)).
rules.notes: Reason codes are listed in EA-3.6.

rules.title: Consequence levels set the error bar
rules.statement: A task type's error bar MUST be set by its consequence level: 0.10 for C1 Low, 0.05 for C2 Moderate and 0.02 for C3 High, while C4 Critical MUST NOT be promoted.
rules.rationale: The more a mistake costs, the more proof is needed before the agent acts alone. Judged actions needed with no errors: 35 (C1), 73 (C2) and 189 (C3).
rules.evidence: The C1 floor freed 45–63% of C1 reviews at 0.60–0.84 escapes per 100 autonomous actions ([research/REPORT-v2.md](../../research/REPORT-v2.md), C2, tag `research/prereg-v2`); the combined policy's reference numbers are in [research/REPORT-v3.md](../../research/REPORT-v3.md).

rules.title: Error bars can only be tightened
rules.statement: The policy owner MAY set a task type's error bar below its consequence level's error bar, and MUST NOT set it above.
rules.rationale: An owner can demand more proof than the default; nobody can demand less.

rules.title: Consequence sets the bar, not the expectation
rules.statement: A task type's consequence level MUST NOT be used to predict how accurate the agent will be, only to set how much accuracy is required.
rules.rationale: Measured errors decide whether the agent meets the bar.
rules.evidence: "Low-risk" task types had the highest error rates (3.8% against 1.3% medium and 1.9% high), so error bars derived from a risk label promoted the most error-prone work ([research/REPORT-v1.md](../../research/REPORT-v1.md), V4, tag `research/prereg-v1`).

rules.title: Evidence doesn't fade with time
rules.statement: Evidence MUST NOT be discounted because of its age.
rules.rationale: At L3 only 5% of actions are judged, so fading evidence demotes good task types on time alone.
rules.evidence: Fading with a 90- or 180-day half-life cost 3.9–6.0 points of automation ([research/REPORT-v2.md](../../research/REPORT-v2.md), F1, tag `research/prereg-v2`).

rules.title: Serialised updates per trust key
rules.statement: Updates to one trust key MUST be applied one at a time, and decisions MUST read the latest committed state.
rules.rationale: Two simultaneous outcomes mustn't both read a stale count.

rules.title: Late incidents apply to the original version
rules.statement: An incident MUST be applied to the trust key and the agent version of the action it refers to, even if the agent has since changed version.
rules.rationale: Evidence belongs to the version that earned it.

rules.title: Task success is an alert, not a gate
rules.statement: Implementations SHOULD alert the AI owner when a task type's task success falls below 85% (C1), 90% (C2) or 95% (C3), and MUST NOT use task success as a condition for promotion.
rules.rationale: An agent that does harmless but incomplete work needs attention, not a frozen ladder.
rules.evidence: As a promotion gate it cost up to 11.8 points of automation for little gain on real agents ([research/REPORT-v2.md](../../research/REPORT-v2.md), C3, tag `research/prereg-v2`).

rules.title: Test passes are not promotion evidence
rules.statement: Passing tests MUST NOT count as judged actions for promotion.
rules.rationale: Tests show the agent changing; spot-checks show the world changing. Only real work earns promotion. Test results may still inform the trust score at a discount (EA-1.18), never the ladder (EA-1.21).
rules.implementation: `engine.py` (tests feed carry-over, and the trust score at their weight, EA-1.18)

rules.title: Trust is measurable at any time from the record
rules.statement: An implementation MUST be able to produce, at any time and from the trust record alone, each trust key's autonomy setting and the human evidence behind it (judged actions and serious errors since its last change).
rules.rationale: Trust you can't look up isn't accountable. Deriving it from the record means anyone can check it.

rules.title: The trust score
rules.statement: An implementation SHOULD report each trust key's trust score: the posterior probability that its true serious-error rate is below its error bar, `I_ε(a₀ + serious, b₀ + judged − serious)` from a Beta(a₀, b₀) prior (default Beta(1, 1)) and the weighted evidence of EA-1.18. A capped task type scores 0.
rules.rationale: One number for "how sure are we this task type is under its bar", comparable across consequence levels.
rules.evidence: With the flat prior, a score of at least 0.975 reproduces the 95% Wilson promotion rule: at every one of the 33 published table cells the score is 0.975–0.979, and it reaches 0.975 at most 1 (C1), 2 (C2) or 7 (C3) judged actions before Wilson promotes. Agreement with Wilson promotion was 99.9–100% at thresholds 0.976–0.979 ([research/REPORT-calibration.md](../../research/REPORT-calibration.md), CAL2). At 0.95 the score promotes about 20% earlier (58 instead of 73 clean at C2) and does not match.
rules.notes: The score is conservative when evidence is thin and slightly over-confident at the top when agents get worse after promotion (ECE 0.039–0.146, [research/REPORT-calibration.md](../../research/REPORT-calibration.md), CAL1). Step-down (EA-2.17) handles the second. Decisions on the Core ladder use the bound or table (EA-2.14, EA-2.15), not the score.

rules.title: The trust profile
rules.statement: An implementation SHOULD report a trust profile for each trust key with: the estimated serious-error rate and a 95% interval; the trust score; the effective evidence (weighted judged actions); the evidence by source; freshness (the agent version and when the last evidence arrived); the trend; the autonomy setting and the autonomy the evidence implies; and whether the evidence is still thin (below the clean floor of EA-2.15).
rules.rationale: One view of everything that justifies a task type's autonomy. A low score with thin evidence means "not enough evidence yet", not "bad agent".
rules.evidence: Most of the score's calibration error is in the low-score bin, where evidence is thin ([research/REPORT-calibration.md](../../research/REPORT-calibration.md), CAL1).
rules.notes: Trend: *slipping* when the Wilson lower bound of the recent window is above the overall rate, *improving* when its upper bound is below it, *stable* otherwise, *insufficient* with fewer than `rolling_window_min` recent judgements.

rules.title: The agent's trust summary
rules.statement: An implementation SHOULD report, for each agent, the share of its actions at each autonomy setting, its incidents (in total and in the last 30 days) and the trend of its task types.
rules.rationale: Owners decide about agents, not trust keys (EA-2.21). This is the view they decide from.

rules.title: Live human judgement is the reference evidence
rules.statement: Live human judgements (pre-review outcomes, spot-check outcomes and incidents) MUST count at weight 1.0, and every other source's weight MUST be stated relative to them.
rules.rationale: People are the standard the agent is held to. Every other source is calibrated against them.
rules.evidence: The Trust Gym's promotion results all use live human evidence (EA-2.14).

rules.title: Other evidence sources are weighted
rules.statement: An implementation MAY count evidence from other sources in the trust score, each at a named, policy-set weight: `shadow` (the agent's output compared with what a person actually did), `replay` (the agent graded on past human-handled cases) and `test` (pre-deployment tests). Defaults: shadow 1.0, replay 1.0, test 0.75. Test results MUST NOT be the only evidence for an implied autonomy above supervised, and any version discount (EA-4.7) MUST apply to every source.
rules.rationale: Evidence that isn't a live review can still say how good an agent is, but it isn't the real work.
rules.evidence: Calibrated weights, 100 observations per key: shadow and replay were at least as informative as a live review (best weight hit the grid maximum of 2.0, which mostly reflects the flat prior's pessimism); tests needed a discount even when graded perfectly, best at 0.75 ([research/REPORT-calibration.md](../../research/REPORT-calibration.md)). Replay found more real errors, with fewer undeserved promotions (3.8% vs 5.3%), but did not speed up ramp-up (CAL3b); shadow increased ramp-up human minutes (CAL3).
rules.notes: Open until the weights are confirmed against human judgement in production (EA-1.19). Live review flatters agents when reviewers miss errors; canaries (EA-3.11) partly correct this.

rules.title: Evidence weights are calibrated against human judgement
rules.statement: An implementation that weights non-human evidence SHOULD calibrate each weight by how well that source agreed with human judgement on the same task type, and SHOULD record the calibration.
rules.rationale: A weight nobody checked is a guess.
rules.notes: Candidate method: choose the weight that minimises the expected calibration error of the trust score against a later human-judged sample.

rules.title: Keep a share of human evidence
rules.statement: An implementation that counts non-human evidence SHOULD alert when weighted human evidence falls below a policy-set share of a trust key's effective evidence (default 20%).
rules.rationale: Other sources drift from real work unless people keep checking it.

rules.title: Other evidence never changes the autonomy setting by itself
rules.statement: Evidence from sources other than live human judgement MUST NOT promote or step down a trust key on the Core ladder; it changes only the trust score and the trust profile.
rules.rationale: Keeps the Core ladder on the tested footing while other sources are still being calibrated.
rules.evidence: Promotion results (EA-2.14) use live human evidence only.

rules.title: Decision order
rules.statement: The decision for a proposed action MUST apply these rules in this order, and the first that matches MUST determine the result: paused (EA-2.2), low tag confidence or unknown type (EA-2.3, EA-2.4), tool floor mismatch (EA-2.5), checks missing or failed (EA-2.6, EA-2.7), capped type (EA-2.8), then level (EA-2.9).
rules.rationale: A fixed order makes every decision reproducible and its reason unambiguous.

rules.title: Paused work is held
rules.statement: A proposed action MUST be held while its agent or its task type is paused.
rules.rationale: Pause is the owner's stop button (EA-3.9).

rules.title: Low-confidence tags are held
rules.statement: A proposed action MUST be held when its tag confidence is below the policy's minimum (default 0.8), whatever the task type's level.
rules.condition: The tagger returns a confidence below `tag_confidence_min`.
rules.rationale: A tagger that isn't sure what kind of work this is shouldn't decide which trust applies.
rules.evidence: A partial defence: it held 4 of 10 adversarial downgrades in v4 study S2b ([research/REPORT-v4.md](../../research/REPORT-v4.md), tag `research/prereg-v4`). The tool floor (EA-2.5) is the main defence.

rules.title: Unknown task types are held
rules.statement: A proposed action tagged with a task type that isn't in the catalogue MUST be held and SHOULD be logged as a candidate new task type.
rules.rationale: Work nobody has defined can't have earned trust.
rules.notes: The reference engine records the `unknown_type` decision; a separate candidate list is not implemented.

rules.title: Floor mismatches are held
rules.statement: A proposed action MUST be held when the floor of any write tool it will call is above the consequence level of its tagged task type.
rules.condition: The action declares at least one write tool.
rules.rationale: Stops a risky action borrowing a low-consequence task type's trust by being tagged, by mistake or on purpose, as that type.
rules.evidence: Removed 100% of autonomous escapes from deliberately mis-tagged actions in all six scenarios, at 0.3–1.8 points of automation; it held all 8 adversarial downgrades that came with a risky write on a real model-based tagger ([research/REPORT-v4.md](../../research/REPORT-v4.md), S2, tag `research/prereg-v4`).
rules.notes: The action's effective consequence is the highest of its tag's level and every write tool's floor.

rules.title: Checks run at every level
rules.statement: Checks MUST run on every proposed action at every trust level, and an action with any failed check MUST be held.
rules.rationale: Trust is about the agent's record; checks catch the obvious mistake in this particular action.
rules.evidence: Earned trust plus checks let through 66–69% fewer serious errors than checks alone at the same automation on real agents ([research/REPORT.md](../../research/REPORT.md), H3, tag `research/prereg`); checks are part of every policy tested since.

rules.title: A missing checks result is a hold
rules.statement: A proposed action MUST be held when no checks result is supplied, unless the policy explicitly allows actions without checks.
rules.rationale: "No checks ran" must never be read as "checks passed".

rules.title: Critical work is always held
rules.statement: A proposed action whose task type is C4 Critical or otherwise capped MUST be held, and such task types MUST NOT be promoted.
rules.rationale: Some actions, such as moving money, deleting records or anything legal or irreversible, are never handed over.
rules.evidence: Consequence levels including "C4 never promotes" were tested in v2 ([research/REPORT-v2.md](../../research/REPORT-v2.md), C2, tag `research/prereg-v2`).

rules.title: The level decides the rest
rules.statement: A proposed action that passes every earlier rule MUST be held if its trust key is at L1 Supervised, and MUST go ahead if its trust key is at L2 Trusted or L3 Senior.
rules.rationale: The core of the ladder.
rules.evidence: 92–100% of promotions were deserved across tiers ([research/REPORT-v3.md](../../research/REPORT-v3.md), reference numbers, tag `research/prereg-v3`).

rules.title: Bundled actions take the most restrictive decision
rules.statement: When one proposal contains several actions, each action MUST be tagged and decided separately, and actions that must happen together MUST all be held if any one of them is held.
rules.rationale: A trusted reply mustn't carry an untrusted record update through with it.

rules.title: Re-decide at execution time
rules.statement: A decision SHOULD be re-evaluated when the action is about to execute, and the newer decision MUST apply if the trust state, a pause or the policy has changed since the action was proposed.
rules.rationale: An action approved before a step-down or a pause shouldn't slip through after it.

rules.title: Every decision is recorded and explainable
rules.statement: Every decision MUST be written to the trust record with its result, its reason, the trust level, the evidence counts, the bound and error bar used, the effective consequence and tool floor, the checks result, and the policy and agent versions.
rules.rationale: Anyone can see why any action was allowed.
rules.evidence: 100% of autonomous actions were explainable from the record in every tier ([research/REPORT.md](../../research/REPORT.md), G2; [research/REPORT-10x.md](../../research/REPORT-10x.md)).

rules.title: New task types start supervised with no evidence
rules.statement: A trust key MUST start at L1 Supervised with no evidence, and MUST NOT inherit evidence from the agent's other task types.
rules.rationale: Earning trust starts from nothing, as it does for a new employee in a new role.
rules.evidence: Pooled evidence across task types did worse than per-type evidence ([research/REPORT-v1.md](../../research/REPORT-v1.md), V3, tag `research/prereg-v1`).

rules.title: Promotion
rules.statement: A trust key below L3 Senior MUST be promoted one level when it has at least `min_judged` (default 30) judged actions since its last level change and the upper bound of its serious-error rate (95% Wilson score interval by default) is at or below its error bar, and MUST NOT be promoted otherwise.
rules.condition: The task type is not C4 Critical or otherwise capped (EA-2.8).
rules.rationale: Promote only when even the plausible worst case is under the bar. With no errors, the worst case is roughly 4 ÷ the number judged.
rules.evidence: 93.3% of promotions were deserved in simulation and 99.6–100% on real agents, with the combined policy on fresh seeds ([research/REPORT-v3.md](../../research/REPORT-v3.md), H1, tag `research/prereg-v3`). The reference engine reproduces the simulation (93.9%).
rules.notes: The upper bound uses all of the key's evidence; the 30-action minimum counts only since the last level change.

rules.title: The Core lookup tables
rules.statement: A Core implementation MAY run promotion and step-down from the published lookup tables instead of computing bounds: promote after the number of judged actions the table gives for the serious errors so far (more than 10: don't promote), and step down when the last 50 judged actions hold at least 10 (C1), 6 (C2) or 3 (C3) serious errors. Tables MUST be derived from the 95% Wilson rule so both give the same decisions.
rules.rationale: A team can run trust from a printed table, with no statistics code.
rules.evidence: Judged actions needed by serious errors 0–10: C1 35 53 69 84 99 113 127 140 153 166 179 · C2 73 110 142 173 202 230 257 284 311 337 363 · C3 189 280 361 437 510 581 650 718 785 851 916 ([research/REPORT-core.md](../../research/REPORT-core.md); [research/core/core-tables.md](../../research/core/core-tables.md)).
rules.notes: The tables differ from the bound only beyond 10 serious errors (the table holds the level) and in the short first window before 50 judgements (the table counts errors, the bound needs `rolling_window_min`).

rules.title: Step-down before promotion, one level at a time
rules.statement: On each new outcome, step-down MUST be evaluated before promotion, and a trust key MUST move at most one level per outcome.
rules.rationale: Dropping all the way to the bottom added nothing over one level, and cost reviews.
rules.evidence: Hard demotion (straight to L1) cut escapes by only 1% against one-level demotion ([research/REPORT.md](../../research/REPORT.md), L4, tag `research/prereg`); one-level demotion was non-inferior ([research/REPORT-v1.md](../../research/REPORT-v1.md), V2, tag `research/prereg-v1`).

rules.title: Step-down on recent errors
rules.statement: A trust key at L2 Trusted or above MUST step down one level when at least `rolling_window_min` (default 10) of its last `rolling_window` (default 50) judged actions are available and the lower bound of their serious-error rate is above its error bar.
rules.rationale: Step down when even the most generous reading of recent work is over the bar. Slow to promote, quick to step down.
rules.evidence: Regressions were caught in a median of 14 actions, 98% within 50 ([research/REPORT-v3.md](../../research/REPORT-v3.md), H4, tag `research/prereg-v3`).
rules.notes: At a 5% bar, 6 serious errors in the last 50 trigger a step-down (the lower bound is 5.6%); 5 do not (4.3%).

rules.title: Incidents step down immediately
rules.statement: An incident MUST count as one serious error and MUST step the action's trust key down one level before the next decision for that key.
rules.rationale: A mistake found after the fact is the clearest evidence there is, and a signal the agent can't game.
rules.evidence: Incidents contained watch-aware agents even when sampling was predictable (median 16 actions) ([research/REPORT-v4.md](../../research/REPORT-v4.md), S3); one level is enough ([research/REPORT-v1.md](../../research/REPORT-v1.md), V2).
rules.notes: An incident adds to the totals but not to the rolling window.

rules.title: Strict promotion (optional)
rules.statement: A policy MAY require strict promotion for chosen consequence levels or task types, in which case promotion MUST use an anytime-valid upper bound (a Beta-binomial mixture confidence sequence with prior Beta(1, 1/ε − 1) and significance 0.05) in place of the Wilson bound.
rules.condition: The policy lists the task type or its consequence level under `strict_promotion`.
rules.rationale: The engine re-checks after every outcome. A bound that stays valid under continuous checking cuts undeserved promotions of steady agents. Recommended for C3 task types and agents with a weak record. Judged actions needed with no errors: 46 (C1), 93 (C2), 236 (C3).
rules.evidence: On real-agent streams it cut undeserved promotions from 2.0% to 0.2% at 28% more evidence; in simulation it barely helped (−6%), because undeserved promotions there came from agents getting worse after promotion ([research/REPORT-v4.md](../../research/REPORT-v4.md), S1, tag `research/prereg-v4`). A fixed 99% Wilson bound or a flat prior cost more evidence for less benefit.
rules.notes: Step-down keeps the rolling Wilson lower bound (EA-2.17).

rules.title: Approval for Senior
rules.statement: A policy MAY require the policy owner to approve promotions to L3 Senior.
rules.rationale: Some organisations want a person to sign off the highest level of autonomy.

rules.title: The decision menu
rules.statement: When an owner reviews an agent or a task type (EA-5.3), the decision SHOULD be one of: increase autonomy, keep, increase oversight, narrow scope, improve (a new version), pause, or retire; and it MUST be recorded.
rules.rationale: A short, fixed menu makes decisions comparable and auditable. Each option maps to a rule: promotion (EA-2.14), step-down or `demote` (EA-2.17), narrowing (EA-5.5), versions (EA-4.1), pause (EA-3.9), retirement (EA-5.4).
rules.implementation: Each option is an engine operation: `promote`, `demote`, `set_spot_rate`, `add_task_type`, `on_version_published`, `pause`, `retire`; each is logged by the governance guard.

rules.title: The dial (optional)
rules.statement: An implementation MAY replace the ladder's fixed levels with a dial: pre-review while the trust score is below 0.975, otherwise spot-check at `clip(5 × (1 − score) + 0.02, 0.02, 1)`. A dial MUST keep the Core step-down and incident rules (EA-2.17, EA-2.18).
rules.rationale: Smooth control: oversight in proportion to uncertainty.
rules.evidence: As safe as the ladder (escapes within +0.02 per 100; regression demotion 17 vs 17 actions; promotions as deserved or more) but it barely raised the work done per human minute (+1% to +7%) ([research/REPORT-dial.md](../../research/REPORT-dial.md), DIAL1 fail, DIAL2–3 pass). The round used a 0.95 pre-review threshold; 0.975 matches Wilson promotion (EA-1.14).
rules.implementation: `stats.py` `dial_spot_rate`; `engine.py` `TrustEngine.trust_report` (`dial`). Decisions in the reference engine follow the ladder.
rules.notes: Core keeps the ladder: it's simpler and costs almost nothing.

rules.title: A decision never reveals sampling
rules.statement: A decision MUST be either hold or act, and MUST NOT indicate whether the action will be spot-checked.
rules.rationale: An agent that knows when it is watched can behave well only then.

rules.title: Spot-checks are drawn after execution
rules.statement: Whether an autonomous action is spot-checked MUST be decided after it executes, at random, at the rate set for its level (default 25% at L2 Trusted and 5% at L3 Senior), using a source of randomness the agent cannot predict.
rules.rationale: Checking never stops, and nobody can tell in advance which actions will be checked.
rules.evidence: With random hidden sampling, the measured error rate matched the true rate (ratio 0.98) and a watch-aware agent was caught in a median of 14 actions ([research/REPORT-v4.md](../../research/REPORT-v4.md), S3, tag `research/prereg-v4`).

rules.title: No fixed sampling schedule
rules.statement: Spot-check selection MUST NOT follow a fixed cadence or any other pattern the agent could learn.
rules.rationale: Predictable checks let a watch-aware agent hide.
rules.evidence: Under a predictable schedule, a watch-aware agent showed reviewers a 1% error rate while really making 18.5%. Without incidents, it went a median of 498 actions before step-down, against 54 under random sampling ([research/REPORT-v4.md](../../research/REPORT-v4.md), S3, tag `research/prereg-v4`).

rules.title: Agents can't see when they're watched
rules.statement: An agent's view of its own trust record MUST exclude spot-check selections, canaries and second checks.
rules.rationale: An agent that can read its record mustn't learn which of its actions are watched.

rules.title: Held actions are reviewable
rules.statement: A held action MUST be shown to reviewers with the proposed action, its checks result, its task type and trust level, and the reason it was held.
rules.rationale: A reviewer can only judge what they can see.

rules.title: Every judgement has a label, and every correction a reason
rules.statement: A reviewer MUST label every judged action with an outcome, and MUST give a reason code for every edit and rejection.
rules.rationale: A reason turns a correction into a rule or test (EA-4.2). Without one, it's only a statistic.

rules.title: Reason codes
rules.statement: Implementations SHOULD use these reason codes: serious ones are `wrong_fact`, `wrong_amount`, `wrong_record`, `wrong_recipient`, `unauthorised_action`, `promise_beyond_policy`, `missing_info_not_asked`, `followed_injected_instruction`, `policy_breach` and `other_serious`; cosmetic ones are `tone`, `wording`, `formatting` and `other_cosmetic`.
rules.rationale: A shared vocabulary makes outcomes comparable across reviewers and organisations.

rules.title: Anyone can report an incident
rules.statement: Every executed action MUST offer a way to report that it was wrong, which records an incident.
rules.rationale: Incidents are the signal an agent can't game (EA-2.18).

rules.title: Anyone affected can challenge
rules.statement: An affected customer or staff member SHOULD be able to challenge any executed action, which opens a review by a person.
rules.rationale: Contestability, and a second channel of evidence.
rules.implementation: none (a product feature; a confirmed challenge becomes an incident)

rules.title: Pause
rules.statement: An authorised person MUST be able to pause an agent or a single task type, which holds every new and not-yet-executed action without undoing executed ones.
rules.rationale: The stop button.

rules.title: Alerts before the bar is crossed
rules.statement: Implementations SHOULD alert the AI owner when a trust key's rolling upper bound passes 80% of its error bar.
rules.rationale: Warn before an automatic step-down.

rules.title: Canaries in review queues
rules.statement: Implementations SHOULD place known-bad canary items in review queues at random, at about 5% of review items.
rules.rationale: People rubber-stamp when they rarely see errors. Canaries keep them sharp and measure them.
rules.evidence: Canaries cut missed errors by 15% in simulation (assumed reviewer model) ([research/REPORT.md](../../research/REPORT.md), G5). At 2%, a poor reviewer stayed trusted for a median of 174 reviews; at 5% they were sorted correctly ([research/REPORT-v2.md](../../research/REPORT-v2.md); [research/REPORT-v3.md](../../research/REPORT-v3.md), R1', tag `research/prereg-v3`).
rules.notes: The policy also has an older `canary_rate` field (0.02); `reviewer_canary_rate` (0.05) is the tested value.

rules.title: Reviewers earn trust too
rules.statement: Each reviewer MUST have a trust key (organisation, reviewer, `review.<task_type>`) whose evidence comes from canaries and second checks, with an error bar of 10% and at least 30 judged items before promotion.
rules.rationale: People follow the same framework as agents. It finds reviewers who need support before their misses reach customers.
rules.evidence: A poor reviewer (60% catch rate) was ever trusted in 9% of simulated organisations; a good one (95%) ended trusted in 100%; escapes fell 15% for 21% more review time ([research/REPORT-v3.md](../../research/REPORT-v3.md), R1', tag `research/prereg-v3`).
rules.notes: Clean second checks count as evidence. Counting only canaries and disagreements never trusted anyone (v2).

rules.title: Second-check rates
rules.statement: A share of each reviewer's decisions MUST be second-checked: about 25% for reviewers at R1 (new) and about 5% for reviewers at R2 (trusted).
rules.rationale: New reviewers are checked more, like new agents.

rules.title: Reviewers step down on misses
rules.statement: A reviewer MUST step down through the same evidence rules as agents (EA-2.17) when they miss canaries or approve actions that later become incidents, and the AI owner SHOULD be told.
rules.rationale: Quality control rather than blame.

rules.title: A second check measures the reviewer only
rules.statement: A second check MUST update only the first reviewer's trust; the corrected agent outcome MUST be recorded separately.
rules.rationale: Keeps reviewer evidence and agent evidence apart.

rules.title: Slowly degrading reviewers (known limitation)
rules.statement: Implementations MAY add a faster check for reviewers whose catch rate declines gradually, such as a rolling window over recent canaries.
rules.rationale: Reviewer trust catches a consistently poor reviewer quickly, but a gradually declining one slowly.
rules.evidence: A reviewer declining from 95% to 50% catch spent a median of about 189 reviews still trusted after falling below 80% ([research/REPORT-v3.md](../../research/REPORT-v3.md), R1').

rules.title: Review windows
rules.statement: An implementation SHOULD set, per task type, how long a held action may wait for review, and MAY batch held actions into reviews that close on size or on time.
rules.rationale: Held work that waits too long costs customers; batches make reviews cheaper per item.
rules.evidence: none yet. Faster and batched reviews are the main lever left on human time ([research/REPORT-dial.md](../../research/REPORT-dial.md)).

rules.title: No action on timeout
rules.statement: A held action MUST NOT execute because nobody reviewed it in time; when a review window passes, the action stays held or is cancelled, and the owner SHOULD be alerted.
rules.rationale: Silence isn't approval (EA-1.2).

rules.title: A pause reaches delegated work (known gap)
rules.statement: Pausing an agent or a task type SHOULD also hold every not-yet-executed action that the paused agent delegated, including actions by agents it started.
rules.rationale: A stop button that stops the principal but not the sub-agents it spawned isn't a stop button. Provenance on delegated actions (EA-8.2) makes this checkable.
rules.evidence: none yet. Raised by reviewers of agentic governance practice (sub-agents outliving a kill switch).
rules.implementation: none yet; `TrustEngine.pause` covers the paused agent's own actions only.
rules.notes: Open question: should a pause reach agents in another organisation that accepted delegated work?

rules.title: Incident response (known gap)
rules.statement: When an incident is reported (EA-3.7), the organisation SHOULD record against it the containment taken, who was notified, the root cause and the remediation, and SHOULD link any rule, check or test changed because of it.
rules.rationale: Today an incident steps the task type down at once (EA-2.18), but the specification says nothing about handling the incident itself. Buyers and regulators expect a documented process.
rules.implementation: none yet; incidents are recorded and step down the task type.
rules.notes: Notification duties under privacy or sector law are outside this specification.

rules.title: Any change is a new version
rules.statement: Any change to an agent's instructions, model, tools or tool scope, rules, checks or knowledge MUST create a new agent version.
rules.rationale: Each of these changes what the agent does, knowledge included.
rules.evidence: none; a definition. Because versions change often, hidden suites (EA-4.5) must run automatically and cheaply.

rules.title: Corrections become draft rules and tests
rules.statement: Every serious error SHOULD produce a draft rule and a draft test whose expected result is the person's corrected action, and both MUST be approved by a person before use.
rules.rationale: The same mistake shouldn't happen twice, and people stay in control of what the agent learns.
rules.evidence: Serious errors fell to about 0% within two to three cycles in five of six agent types ([research/REPORT.md](../../research/REPORT.md), learning loop); on the commercial harness the loop plus tool scope cut serious errors 82–87% ([research/REPORT-10x.md](../../research/REPORT-10x.md), X6, tag `research/prereg-10x-d`). Synthetic tasks; the weak agent was missing rules by design.

rules.title: Training and hidden split
rules.statement: Approved correction tests MUST be assigned at random, about two thirds to the training suite and one third to the hidden suite.
rules.rationale: The hidden third judges new versions on mistakes the improver never saw.
rules.evidence: Hidden-test pass rates tracked the true error rate (Spearman ρ = −0.81 across 36 versions), and 117% of the training gain carried over to hidden tests: no sign of test-gaming ([research/REPORT.md](../../research/REPORT.md), H6 and H7, tag `research/prereg`).

rules.title: Hidden tests stay hidden
rules.statement: Hidden tests MUST NOT be readable by the agent or by anyone or anything that changes the agent.
rules.rationale: A test the improver can see stops measuring anything.

rules.title: New versions are tested before going live
rules.statement: A new agent version MUST run its training and hidden suites for every task type before it goes live, and the results MUST be recorded.
rules.rationale: Carry-over (EA-4.6) depends on them.

rules.title: Carry-over
rules.statement: A trust key MUST keep all its evidence through a version change when the new version passes at least `carry_hidden_min` (default 0.8) of that task type's hidden tests and the hidden suite has at least 10 tests.
rules.rationale: An improvement that passes tests it has never seen shouldn't cost the agent its record.
rules.evidence: Learning agents went from 0 of 400 to 142 of 400 task types promoted, with every promotion deserved and no escapes ([research/REPORT-v1.md](../../research/REPORT-v1.md), V1, tag `research/prereg-v1`). On fresh seeds it was safe, but kept only about half the autonomy with realistic hidden tests and about 90% with sharp ones ([research/REPORT-v3.md](../../research/REPORT-v3.md), K1', tag `research/prereg-v3`). On the commercial harness, suites never reached 10 tests, so it never applied ([research/REPORT-10x.md](../../research/REPORT-10x.md)).
rules.notes: An earlier condition, "no worse than the previous version's score", was removed in v0.3: it added noise without safety.

rules.title: Version discount
rules.statement: When carry-over doesn't apply, a trust key's judged-action and serious-error counts MUST be multiplied by `version_discount` (default 0.5), and the key MUST drop to L1 if its upper bound then exceeds its error bar.
rules.rationale: A changed agent is a new hire with a CV: some credit, not all. A long record survives a failed change; a fresh promotion doesn't.
rules.evidence: Part of every policy tested from v0 ([research/REPORT.md](../../research/REPORT.md)); see EA-4.6.

rules.title: Unannounced versions are untested
rules.statement: An action from an agent version that was never published through the version process MUST be treated as coming from an untested version, with the version discount applied.
rules.rationale: Skipping the tests mustn't keep the trust.

rules.title: Version results apply per agent
rules.statement: A version's test results MUST apply to that agent's trust keys in every organisation, and task types missing from the results MUST receive the version discount.
rules.rationale: The same agent version behaves the same everywhere; untested task types are untested.

rules.title: Seeded hidden tests per version (optional)
rules.statement: An organisation MAY seed each task type's hidden suite with scenarios written for a new version, and seeded tests MUST have the same protections as correction-based hidden tests.
rules.rationale: Correction-based suites dry up once an agent gets good: few mistakes means few new tests, so carry-over can't apply.
rules.evidence: On the commercial harness no hidden suite reached the 10-test minimum, so every version change halved the record ([research/REPORT-10x.md](../../research/REPORT-10x.md)). Whether written tests predict real errors as well as correction-based ones needs its own study.
rules.notes: A seeded test is a realistic request plus the expected outcome, written by the policy owner or AI owner or drawn from past human-handled cases, and never written by the agent or its improver. Replace a share each release.

rules.title: Batch changes into releases
rules.statement: Knowledge edits and corrections SHOULD be batched into regular, tested releases, for example weekly.
rules.rationale: Each version change is a chance to lose evidence. Fewer, better-tested versions keep more of it.
rules.evidence: With 20% of edits making the agent worse, automation stayed near 13% whatever the carry-over rule ([research/REPORT-v2.md](../../research/REPORT-v2.md), K1).

rules.title: Rollback is a new version
rules.statement: Republishing an earlier agent version MUST be treated as a new version change.
rules.rationale: The world may have moved since that version last ran.

rules.title: The agent can't change what it's judged by
rules.statement: An agent, and any automated process that improves it, MUST NOT be able to change its tests, checks, policy or trust record.
rules.rationale: No marking its own homework.
rules.evidence: All 28 self-promotion and rule-loosening attempts were blocked, with all 8 legitimate requests allowed ([research/REPORT.md](../../research/REPORT.md), G4).

rules.title: Upstream model changes are new versions (known gap)
rules.statement: A change to the model an agent runs on, including one its provider makes without notice, SHOULD be treated as a new agent version (EA-4.1), and an implementation SHOULD detect it wherever the provider exposes a model identifier.
rules.rationale: Trust is earned by a specific version. A silent model swap is a version change nobody recorded, so the record would credit the new model with the old model's evidence.
rules.notes: Input-distribution drift (the work changing, not the agent) is caught only indirectly, by continuous spot-checks (EA-3.1) and step-down (EA-2.17).

rules.title: Re-entry after a long gap
rules.statement: A trust key at L2 Trusted or above MUST step down one level when its task type is used again after a gap of more than `reentry_gap_days` (default 60).
rules.rationale: After a long break the world may have changed.
rules.evidence: Cut escapes after drift by 17% at no automation cost, on fresh seeds ([research/REPORT-v3.md](../../research/REPORT-v3.md), F1', tag `research/prereg-v3`).

rules.title: Rare task types (known limitation)
rules.statement: Implementations MAY keep rare task types supervised indefinitely, and SHOULD NOT promote a task type on evidence other than judged actions until a method for rare task types is tested.
rules.rationale: Time to promotion depends on frequency. At C2 (73 judged actions), a task done 10 times a day is promoted in about a week, 10 times a month in about 7 months, and twice a month in about 3 years: in practice, never. The re-entry rule (EA-5.1) compounds this. Review cost is proportional to frequency, so rare task types cost little to keep supervised, and for high-consequence rare work the lack of evidence is itself a reason to keep a person involved.
rules.evidence: none yet. Candidates to test: - **Historical replay:** the agent in shadow on past human-handled cases, counted at a discount (e.g. 0.5). - **Other organisations:** evidence for the same agent version on the same task type elsewhere, discounted. This differs from pooling across different task types, which failed. - **Frequency-aware re-entry:** step down only after more than 60 days *and* more than about 3× the task type's usual interval.
rules.notes: Test passes are not a candidate. Tests show the agent changing, not real work (EA-1.12). Replay and shadow evidence now feed the trust score (EA-1.18), but not the ladder (EA-1.21).

rules.title: Periodic agent review
rules.statement: The AI owner SHOULD review each agent at least quarterly: its levels per task type, incidents, drift and scope.
rules.rationale: Is the scope still right, and is the agent still needed?

rules.title: Retiring a task type
rules.statement: Retiring a task type for an agent MUST hold every new action of that type and MUST be recorded; its evidence stays in the record.
rules.rationale: Stopping work should be as accountable as starting it.

rules.title: Narrowing scope is a policy change
rules.statement: Narrowing a task type's scope or splitting it MUST be a recorded policy change, and each new task type MUST start supervised with no evidence (EA-2.13).
rules.rationale: A narrower task is a different task. Its trust must be earned on its own (EA-7.2).

rules.title: Bringing a task type back
rules.statement: A retired task type that is brought back MUST start supervised, with its earlier evidence discounted as for a new version (EA-4.7).
rules.rationale: The world and the agent may both have changed while it was retired.

rules.title: Roles and a named owner
rules.statement: Every agent MUST have a named AI owner, and implementations MUST distinguish the roles AI owner, policy owner, reviewer, auditor and builder.
rules.rationale: Accountability belongs to a person, never to "the system".
rules.notes: - **AI owner:** a team lead, department head or similar. Owns the agent, its task catalogue and consequence levels. - **Policy owner:** sets error bars, caps, tool scope and sample rates. - **Reviewer:** judges outcomes. - **Auditor:** reads everything and changes nothing. - **Builder:** changes agent versions.

rules.title: The AI owner maintains the task catalogue
rules.statement: The AI owner for an area MUST maintain its task catalogue and assign each task type's consequence level; a tagger MAY propose new task types, which take effect only when the AI owner accepts them.
rules.rationale: The person accountable for the work decides how it is divided and how much proof each part needs.

rules.title: Agents can't govern themselves
rules.statement: An agent MUST NOT be able to change its own trust, tests, checks, policy or trust record, though it MAY read its own record as filtered by EA-3.3.
rules.rationale: No self-promotion.

rules.title: Separation of duties
rules.statement: A builder of an agent MUST NOT approve that agent's promotions, change its error bars, caps or sample rates, or edit its tests or checks.
rules.rationale: Nobody approves their own work.

rules.title: Every governance request is logged
rules.statement: Every request to change policy, trust, tests or checks MUST name the person or system making it and MUST be written to the trust record, whether it is allowed or blocked.
rules.rationale: Blocked attempts are evidence too.

rules.title: Policy is versioned and takes effect immediately
rules.statement: Every policy change MUST create a new policy version that takes effect immediately; a lower error bar MUST be re-evaluated against every affected trust key at once, dropping keys whose bound no longer holds to L1, while a higher error bar MUST only take effect at each key's next outcome.
rules.rationale: A stricter rule protects immediately; a looser one is earned.
rules.notes: A newly capped task type also drops to L1.

rules.title: The record is append-only
rules.statement: The trust record MUST be append-only, with no way to edit or delete an entry.
rules.rationale: It is the agent's whole employment history.
rules.implementation: `record.py` `TrustRecord` (no edit API; SQLite triggers refuse updates and deletes)

rules.title: The record is tamper-evident
rules.statement: Each record entry MUST include a SHA-256 hash of its canonical JSON and of the previous entry's hash, and verification MUST detect any edited, deleted or reordered entry.
rules.rationale: Regulated buyers need history that provably hasn't been altered.

rules.title: State is rebuilt from the record
rules.statement: Replaying the trust record from empty MUST reproduce every trust state exactly.
rules.rationale: The record is the truth; state is only a cache of it.

rules.title: Sequence, not time, orders the record
rules.statement: The trust record's order MUST be each entry's sequence number in the hash chain, and replay, scans and audits MUST NOT order entries by timestamp.
rules.rationale: Clocks drift and servers disagree.

rules.title: One exact timestamp format
rules.statement: Every timestamp in the trust record MUST be ISO 8601 in UTC with exactly three digits of milliseconds and a `Z` suffix (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ`), other ISO 8601 forms with a time zone MUST be normalised to it when read, and timestamps with no time zone MUST be rejected.
rules.rationale: - Auditors can read it at a glance. - UTC has no daylight-saving ambiguity: Melbourne's local clock repeats an hour each April. - One fixed format keeps the hash chain stable, since the same moment always produces the same bytes.
rules.notes: Products show local time; storage is UTC. A zero-millisecond moment still prints `.000Z`.

rules.title: Epoch time stays at the edges
rules.statement: Epoch milliseconds MAY be used in interfaces and internal code if the name says so in full (for example `created_at_epoch_milliseconds`), and MUST be converted before anything enters the trust record.
rules.rationale: Convenient for maths, unreadable in an audit.

rules.title: The record is kept permanently
rules.statement: The trust record and every decision MUST be retained permanently.
rules.rationale: It is the evidence behind every level, for agents and reviewers alike.

rules.title: References and labels, not customer content
rules.statement: The trust record MUST hold references, labels and hashes only (action identifiers, task types, outcomes, reason codes, versions, actor identifiers and a payload hash), and MUST NOT hold customer content such as messages, names or amounts.
rules.rationale: Privacy law (in Australia, Australian Privacy Principle 11.2) requires personal information to be destroyed or de-identified once it's no longer needed. Content stays in the source system under its normal retention; the permanent record loses nothing it needs when that content is deleted.
rules.evidence: none; a legal and design decision.

rules.title: Records follow the schema
rules.statement: Proposed actions, decisions, outcome events, trust states, policies and record entries MUST validate against the JSON Schemas in [`schema/`](../schema/).
rules.rationale: One source of truth for the data model, so other implementations interoperate.

rules.title: Provider and deployer (known gap)
rules.statement: When the agent's provider and the organisation deploying it are different parties, the roles in EA-6.1 SHOULD be assigned to a named person in each party in writing, and both parties SHOULD be able to read the record for the agent's actions in the deploying organisation.
rules.rationale: The specification treats the organisation as one party. In B2B deployments the hardest question is who owns what when an agent acts across both parties' systems; it must be settled before the agent acts, not after an incident.
rules.notes: Open questions: who may pause (EA-3.9), who sets consequence levels, and whether trust earned with one deployer may inform another (EA-1.1 says no).

rules.title: Task types are catalogue entries
rules.statement: Each task type MUST be defined as a catalogue entry with a name, a description of what is in and out of scope, three to five example requests, the tools it may use, and a consequence level.
rules.rationale: The tagger and the reviewers work from the description and examples, not the name. The tools and consequence level drive tool scope (EA-7.7) and the error bar (EA-1.5).
rules.evidence: In v4 study S2b, adversarial phrasing steered a model-based tagger to a lower-consequence type 3.3% of the time (1 of 300 without adversarial phrasing). See [research/REPORT-v4.md](../../research/REPORT-v4.md), tag `research/prereg-v4`.
rules.notes: Schema: [`schema/policy.schema.json`](../schema/policy.schema.json).

rules.title: Split task types only when consequence or error rate differs
rules.statement: A task type SHOULD be split into two only when the consequence of a mistake differs or the agent's measured error rate clearly differs between them, and SHOULD NOT be split because of wording alone.
rules.rationale: Each task type earns trust from scratch (35 to 189 judged actions, EA-1.5). Too many types slow everything down; too few mix good and bad work.
rules.evidence: Too coarse: 7% automation against 27% ([research/REPORT.md](../../research/REPORT.md), L3). Borrowing across types hurt ([research/REPORT-v1.md](../../research/REPORT-v1.md), V3). Too fine is a consequence of EA-1.5's evidence floors.

rules.title: Task-type names are keys only
rules.statement: Task-type names SHOULD follow the shape `<domain>.<object>.<verb>` (for example `customer_service.refund.issue`), and the name MUST NOT affect the trust calculation.
rules.rationale: The shape lets reports roll up by domain and object, maps naturally to tools and permissions, and lets defaults be set per domain. It is a convention, not a rule of the maths.

rules.title: No parameters in task-type names
rules.statement: Task-type names SHOULD NOT encode parameters such as amounts; risk that depends on arguments SHOULD be expressed with an argument-dependent tool floor (EA-7.8).
rules.rationale: `refund.issue_over_200` multiplies the catalogue and splits evidence. An argument-dependent floor holds the large refunds without a new type.

rules.title: Every proposed action is tagged
rules.statement: Every proposed action MUST be tagged with a task type and a confidence before a decision is made.
rules.rationale: Trust is looked up by task type; an untagged action has no trust to look up.

rules.title: Tag from descriptions and examples
rules.statement: A tagger SHOULD classify actions using the task types' descriptions and examples, not their names alone.
rules.rationale: Descriptions and examples say what's in scope; names don't.
rules.evidence: Indirect: v4 study S2b measured mis-tagging under adversarial phrasing ([research/REPORT-v4.md](../../research/REPORT-v4.md)). A study comparing names-only against descriptions-and-examples is future work.

rules.title: Tool scope per task type
rules.statement: An agent working on a task type MUST be offered only the tools listed for that task type.
rules.rationale: Tools the work doesn't need are a source of mistakes and an attack surface for injected instructions.
rules.evidence: Wrong or unneeded tool calls fell 73% (0.519 to 0.141 per task) with no loss of task success (96.2% to 95.6%); serious errors fell from 2.0% to 0.67% ([research/REPORT.md](../../research/REPORT.md), L1, tag `research/prereg`). On the commercial harness, tool scope plus the learning loop cut serious errors 82–87% ([research/REPORT-10x.md](../../research/REPORT-10x.md), X6, tag `research/prereg-10x-d`).

rules.title: Every write tool has a floor consequence
rules.statement: Every write tool MUST have a floor consequence equal to the highest consequence level of any task type that lists it, or C4 Critical if no task type lists it, unless the policy owner sets an explicit floor or an argument-dependent floor function applies.
rules.rationale: A tool that can do high-consequence things carries that consequence wherever it is used.

rules.title: Don't share write tools across consequence levels
rules.statement: A write tool SHOULD NOT be listed by task types of different consequence levels; implementations SHOULD warn when one is.
rules.rationale: A shared tool pulls every task that uses it up to its highest consequence, so the low-consequence task can never earn autonomy.
rules.evidence: In v4, a shared `send_email` (used for C1 reminders and C3 offers) pushed reminders to C3 ([research/REPORT-v4.md](../../research/REPORT-v4.md), recommended change 2). Split such tools (`send_reminder`, `send_offer`) or give them argument-dependent floors.

rules.title: Every action comes with a checks result
rules.statement: The agent's platform MUST supply the result of its checks with every proposed action; a missing result MUST be treated as a failed check (EA-2.7).
rules.rationale: Checks are the agent's own acceptance criteria. Which checks to run is up to its builders; that a result exists is not.

rules.title: Every action carries a version
rules.statement: Every proposed action MUST carry the identifier of the agent version that produced it.
rules.rationale: Trust follows the version (EA-4.1, EA-4.7). Without a version, no change can be detected.

rules.title: Delegation never adds authority
rules.statement: When agent A delegates an action of task type T to agent B, B's effective level for that action MUST be the lower of A's and B's levels for T, and the action MUST be held if A has no level for T.
rules.rationale: A trusted agent can't use a junior one to do what it couldn't do itself, and vice versa.

rules.title: Delegated actions carry their provenance
rules.statement: Every delegated action MUST carry the identifier of the action that delegated it, and serious errors SHOULD count against the agent whose output was changed.
rules.rationale: Blame follows the edit. Agents further up the chain get a "missed it" mark, tracked but not yet counted.

rules.title: Peer reliability with exploration
rules.statement: When an agent routes work to peer agents by reliability, routing SHOULD use Thompson sampling over per-(agent, skill) Beta posteriors with a forgetting factor of 0.98, SHOULD verify answers whose lower bound is under 0.85, and SHOULD audit 10% of answers at random.
rules.rationale: Always routing to the most-trusted peer never tests the others, so a peer that turns bad stays first choice.
rules.evidence: 95–96% accuracy with under half the verification calls ([research/REPORT-v1.md](../../research/REPORT-v1.md), V5, tag `research/prereg-v1`). A peer that turns bad is caught only after a median of 21 bad outputs with forgetting (37.5 without), above the 10 targeted.

rules.title: Keep consequential peer work supervised
rules.statement: Actions one agent takes on another agent's output SHOULD stay at L1 Supervised for C2 and higher consequence levels.
rules.rationale: Peer reliability tracking is slow to detect a peer that turns bad (EA-8.3).

rules.title: Reviewer agents earn trust as their own task type
rules.statement: An agent that reviews another agent's work MUST be treated as performing its own task type (`review.<agent>`) with its own trust key, SHOULD be used only to triage agents with low error rates, and MUST NOT be assumed more reliable because it uses a different model.
rules.rationale: Reviewing is work that earns trust like any other.
rules.evidence: - **Low-error agent:** a reviewer agent removed 71% of human reviews safely. - **High-error agent:** not safe; escapes rose from 0.86 to 2.56 per 100. - **Different model:** recall was lower (82.9% against 87.4%) with nearly double the false alarms. Source: [research/REPORT.md](../../research/REPORT.md), M1 and M2, tag `research/prereg`.
